thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Turn Negative Ahead of FOMC Policy Statement

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Turn Negative Ahead of FOMC Policy Statement
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Wednesday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.4%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.6%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.4%
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): -1.4%
PowerShares QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -0.5%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 0.5%.
U.S. stocks were mostly lower at session's half, ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee's policy statement at 2 pm ET.
The Federal Open Markets Committee concludes its two-day policy meeting this afternoon and will issue a release at 2 pm ET. Stifel expects a "benign" announcement as it's forecast to hold its federal funds rate at 1.75%.
"The statement, furthermore, is expected to reiterate a positive outlook for both growth and inflation, as well as reaffirm a commitment to a continued "gradual" pace of policy adjustment," Stifel said in a note on Wednesday. "Some, however, anticipate the statement to offer hints of a commitment to a June rate hike and a potentially faster pace of rate hikes in the remaining eight months of the year. On the other hand, describing the inflation goal as "symmetric" -- as in every statement since March 2017 -- may reinforce the view the Fed can be patient."
Upbeat earnings from Apple (AAPL) which helped buoy sentiment earlier, was overshadowed by other companies reporting lackluster results. Snap (SNAP) shares plunged 20% after the company said revenue rose to $230.7 million, missing consensus for a gain to $244.6 million. Molson Coors Brewing (TAP) was down some 13% after reporting that demand for alcoholic beverages decline in the first quarter. U.S. brand volume dropped 3.8% from last year while global demand declined 3.1%, the company said.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 0.02% while other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were lower.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 0.7% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.7%.
Snap (SNAP) shares fell more than 20% after the social media company reported a Q1 non-GAAP diluted net loss per share of $0.17, in line with the consensus on Capital IQ and compared with the loss a year earlier of $0.20. Revenue rose 54% to $230.7 million, but that missed views for $244.6 million. Daily active users were up 15% year on year to 191 million and were up 2% on a quarterly basis.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.5%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 1% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 1.4%.
Mastercard (MA) rose 3% after the firm said it beat analysts' expectations in Q1 on both the top and bottom lines as revenue surged 31% to a record high on an increase in transactions for the credit-card company. Adjusted diluted earnings per share jumped to $1.50 from $1.01 a year earlier. That beat the consensus of analysts polled by Capital IQ for $1.24. Revenue climbed to $3.6 billion, also ahead of the Wall Street projection for $3.26 billion.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.7% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.6%.
HollyFrontier (HFC) rose more than 6% after the firm reported Q1 adjusted earnings of $0.77 per share, excluding one-time items, compared with the prior-year period's $0.19 loss per share. Analysts polled by Capital IQ were expecting EPS of $0.39. Revenue was $4.13 billion, up from $3.08 billion in the same quarter last year. The Street view is for revenue of $3.30 billion.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) fell 1.2% and other industrial funds Vanguard Industrials (VIS) and iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), were in the red.
Littelfuse (LFUS) rose more than 14% after the company reported Q1 adjusted diluted EPS of $2.39 increased 41% over last year, surpassing the $1.81 average estimate of analysts surveyed by Capital IQ. Q1 sales rose 46% to $417.8 million from $285.4 million last year, exceeding the analyst consensus of $391.2 million. The company said adjusted diluted EPS are expected to range from $2.39 to $2.53 in the second quarter, a 17% growth over the prior-year quarter at the midpoint. The Street view is at $2.23.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.2%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.1%. Natural gas was up 1.7% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.7%.
Gold was up 0.1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.7%. Silver was down 1.7%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 1.3%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 1.2% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were firmer.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 1% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in negative territory.
Estee Lauder (EL) fell more than 6% after the cosmetics maker reported fiscal Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.17 compared with adjusted EPS of $0.90 a year earlier and exceeding the $1.07 average estimate by analysts in a Capital IQ survey. Net sales for the quarter ended March 31 totaled $3.37 billion, an increase from $2.86 billion a year earlier. The analyst consensus was $3.25 billion. The cosmetics company expects net sales to grow between 11% and 12% in constant currency and reported net sales to grow between 15% and 16%. The fiscal 2017 acquisitions of Too Faced and BECCA are expected to contribute about 2 percentage points of incremental sales growth. Full-year adjusted earnings per share are projected to be between $4.38 and $4.42, in line to slightly above the $4.38 per share consensus.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.01% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 1.5%.
LivaNova (LIVN) fell 9% to the lowest since early January even as the company posted adjusted Q1 EPS of $0.68 compared with $0.67 a year earlier and beating the $0.65 average estimate by analysts in a Capital IQ poll. Revenue was $250.4 million compared with $226.8 million a year earlier. That was higher than the $245.2 million analyst consensus. LivaNova expects worldwide net sales for the full-year to grow between 6% and 8% on a constant currency basis instead of the 4% to 6% growth it predicted in February. It sees adjusted EPS for 2018 in the range of $3.50 to $3.70, rather than the $3.40 to $3.60 estimate given in February.
